slides.title: “You need 20% down.”
slides.subtitle: Not in Canada. Here's what the down payment rules actually say.

slides.title: As little as 5% down
slides.body: On a home priced at $500,000 or less, the minimum down payment is 5% of the purchase price.

slides.title: It's tiered
slides.body: 5% of the first $500,000, plus 10% of the portion of the price above $500,000.

slides.title: $1.5 million and up
slides.body: Homes priced at $1.5 million or more need at least 20% down.

slides.title: Mortgage loan insurance
slides.body: With less than 20% down, you'll typically need mortgage loan insurance. The premium can be paid up front or added to your mortgage.

slides.title: 30-year amortizations
slides.body: Since Dec 15, 2024, first-time buyers can get up to 30 years on an insured mortgage. Lower monthly payments, but more interest overall.

slides.title: Want to know your numbers?
slides.body: I can set you up with an appointment with a qualified mortgage professional. Just send me a message.

caption:
First-time home buyer in BC? You don't need 20% down to buy a home in Canada.

The federal minimums:
🏠 $500,000 or less: 5% of the price
🏠 $500,000 to $1.5M: 5% of the first $500K + 10% of the rest
🏠 $1.5M and up: 20%

Example: on a $600,000 home, the minimum is $35,000 (about 5.8%), not $120,000.

The catch: under 20% down you'll typically need mortgage loan insurance. The premium can be paid up front or added to your mortgage. And first-time buyers can now get up to a 30-year amortization on an insured mortgage — lower payments, more interest over time.

Everyone's situation is different. Want to know your own numbers? I can set you up with an appointment with a qualified mortgage professional. Just send me a DM.
